chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zurara ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who bought a pasture to graze in for fifty dirhams, or less or more, so he intended to include with him anyone who would graze in it and take the price from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him include with him whoever he wishes for part of what he gave, and even if he includes with him forty-nine [sheep], and his own sheep is one dirham, there is no problem.'
And if he grazed in it before he lets them in, for a month or two months or more than that, after making it clear to them, there is no problem.

And it is not for him to sell it for fifty dirhams and graze with them, nor for more than fifty and not graze with them, unless he has done work in the pasture, such as digging a well or cutting a canal, or he exerted himself in it with the consent of the owners of the pasture. So there is no problem with him selling it for more than what he bought it for, because he has done work in it, and because of that it is valid for him.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for sub-leasing a pasture or land in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the permissibility of sub-leasing (*Ijarah*) and profit-sharing in agricultural contexts, emphasizing that the owner may include others in the grazing rights for a proportional share of the cost. It further clarifies that selling the pasture at a higher price is valid if the owner has invested labor or capital, such as digging a well, with the consent of the stakeholders, thereby establishing a principle of fair value addition in Shia commercial jurisprudence. The text highlights the flexibility in contractual terms, allowing for varied financial arrangements as long as the core lease agreement is respected and improvements are acknowledged.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from his brother Al Hassan, from Zurara Bin Muhammad, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who bought a pasture field to pasture in, for fifty Dirhams, or less or more. So he intended that he includes with him anyone who would pasture in it and take the price from him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him include with him the ones who he so desires to for part of what he has given, and even if he were to include with him forty nine sheep, and there was (only one) sheep of his for one Dirham, so there is no problem.
And if he was to pasture therein before he enters (others therein) by a month, or two months, or more than that after clears it for them, so there is no problem,

and it is not for him that he sells it for fifty Dirhams and he pastures along with them, nor for more than fifty Dirham and he does not pasture along with them, unless it so happens that he had worked in the pasture with a work, digging a well, or grooving a canal, or he gets exhausted therein with the agreement of the owner of the pasture, so there is no problem with him selling it for more than what he had bought it for, because he had worked therein with a work. Thus, due to that, it is correct for him’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from his brother, al-Hassan from Zur’ah ibn Muhammad from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“Upon asking him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who buys a pasture for fifty dirham or less or more and he wants to allow entering the pasture whoever wants to enter so that he charges them for it. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can allow whomever he wants with a payment of part of what he has paid. If he enters the pasture with a payment of forty-nine and his sheep (graze) for one dirham, it is not unlawful.
He cannot receive payment of fifty dirham and his sheep graze along with them or for more than fifty but his sheep do not graze with them,

unless he has done a certain work in the pasture, like digging a well, or a canal or has experienced fatigue in it with the consent of the owners of the pasture, in which case it is not unlawful to sell it for more than for what he has bought, because he has done certain work in it and with this it becomes valid for him.’”
